chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan and ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad narrated to me, from al-ʿUbaydī, from Yūnus, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two عليهما السلام.

He said: He was asked about a man who joined the Imam in his salat (prayer) after the Imam had preceded him by one rakʿah. When the Imam finished, he left with the people, then remembered that he had missed one rakʿah. He said: He repeats one rakʿah only; that is permissible for him so long as he has not turned his face away from the qiblah. But if he has turned his face, then he must begin the salat (prayer) anew.

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), referring to the congregational prayer being performed
key_terms.يَسْتَقْبِلَ: he begins afresh or recommences from the start

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he remembers after the Imam finishes that he missed one rakʿah in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a follower in congregational salat (prayer) who realizes after the Imam finishes that he has missed one rakʿah. If he has not yet turned away from the qiblah, he may complete the missed rakʿah; if he has turned away, he must restart the salat (prayer).
